assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observation of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos in a cubic-kilometre Antarctic detector opened neutrino astronomy as an observational field. It required an instrumental concept (deep-ice optical detection) that was unproven when pursued and has since delivered the diffuse flux, an evolving source picture and a multi-messenger association. Clear, original and foundational for astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen drove the concept and realisation of IceCube; Spiering was a central figure in the earlier Baikal and AMANDA/IceCube development and in the collaboration's scientific leadership. Karle was a major contributor to AMANDA/IceCube construction and operations. Any trio omits many collaboration members and the earlier DUMAND and Baikal pioneers, so the selection is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse high-energy flux has been confirmed by independent analyses and channels within IceCube and is supported by other telescopes' results. Source identification is still partial, but the discovery of the flux itself is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the supplied credit list adequately captures the pioneers (DUMAND, Baikal, AMANDA) is my uncertain recollection and I have not verified it.
Source identification remains incomplete, so a prize would rest on the flux discovery rather than a settled source picture.
The result comes from a single large collaboration, with limited fully independent confirmation from a second large detector.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, has delivered the best frequency standards ever built, with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. It is a decisive measurement-science advance with clear applications to relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a prospective redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised early strontium clocks; Ye's group drove the performance to the highest precision and demonstrated key systematic control. Two laureates give a clean, fair attribution, though Hall-Hansch comb work and Hall's earlier prize provide context.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories (Japan, USA, Europe) have reproduced and surpassed the initial performance. The technology is mature, and recognition is timely, with redefinition of the second still pending.
uncertainties: Whether other contributors to lattice-clock theory and ion-clock competitors (whose work is not on this ballot) should share recognition is unclear.
Practical redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, so impact is partly prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the subsequent experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter. It is original, clear and has spawned a very large body of confirming and extending work.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental observation. Theory-experiment pairing fits a three-person structure, though the Cao et al. first author, and other groups (including related earlier theory by others), are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups across several moire systems, though the microscopic origin of the superconductivity remains debated. Recognition is timely and likely to strengthen.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity in the twisted system is not settled.
Earlier theoretical work on twisted bilayers by other authors may complicate priority; I cannot verify that.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold-atom quantum simulation of Hubbard-type models, from the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition to quantum gas microscopes, has turned strongly correlated many-body physics into an engineered, controllable experiment. Its conceptual and technical impact on many-body and quantum-information physics is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied the theoretical framework for cold-atom quantum simulation and lattice proposals; Bloch and Greiner realised the Mott transition and single-site microscopy. Esslinger's Fermi-Hubbard realisations are also strong, so the choice among four credited names is difficult and the Mott-transition credit also involves Hansch and Greiner's collaborators.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended by many groups worldwide. The field is mature and productive, although the quantum-simulation payoff for open problems is still being demonstrated.
uncertainties: Which of Bloch, Esslinger and Greiner has the strongest claim, given overlapping experimental breakthroughs, is unresolved.
The extent to which simulation has solved a problem inaccessible to classical computation remains debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution made secure communication grounded in the laws of physics, linking foundations of quantum mechanics (entanglement, no-cloning) to a technology now deployed in commercial links and satellites. The ideas are original, clear and enduring.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced the BB84 protocol; Ekert independently proposed the entanglement-based protocol. This is a natural three-person structure with well-documented priority, although Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known precursor.
assessment.maturity: Protocols have been implemented widely, including satellite links. The 2022 prize recognised the underlying entanglement experiments, which some may see as partial overlap. Practical security under real-device imperfections is still an active area.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests.
Whether the field is judged a physics discovery or an information-science invention is unsettled.
Wiesner's precursor role is something I recall but have not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators introduced a new classification of quantum phases and generated a major experimental field, with HgTe quantum wells providing the first confirmation. Importance and originality are high, building on the 2016 prize's topological theme.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group realised the experimental observation in HgTe following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's prediction. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D topological insulator discoveries are not on this entry, so credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in many materials. The concept is mature, with some overlap with the earlier Nobel recognition of topological phases.
uncertainties: Omission of the BHZ prediction and 3D topological insulator experimental work leaves attribution unresolved.
Partial overlap with the 2016 prize may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon pixel detectors enabled precise vertexing and tracking in high-rate collider environments, and underpin discoveries from heavy-flavour physics to Higgs measurements. As an experimentalist who builds instruments, I regard the enabling role of such devices as under-recognised, though the Nobel criterion is a discovery or invention of great importance, and this clearly is an invention with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Heijne developed early hybrid pixel concepts at CERN; Parker developed microstrip and pixel detectors; Snoeys contributed monolithic and readout-electronics advances. The instrument was developed by large teams, so fair credit among many (including others not listed) is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Widely deployed at LHC and elsewhere, a mature and independently validated technology. Timing is reasonable, though a prize would likely be viewed as for instrumentation rather than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Collaborative nature of the development makes a three-person attribution contestable.
My professional proximity to detector instrumentation could bias me, so I discount this slightly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser, based on intersubband transitions engineered in semiconductor heterostructures, created a compact mid-infrared and terahertz source with wide use in spectroscopy and sensing. It is a clear, original invention validated over three decades.
assessment.attribution: Faist and Capasso led the Bell Labs team that demonstrated the first device in 1994, with Cho's molecular-beam epitaxy growth essential. Cho could be a third name; Kazarinov and Suris's earlier proposal for the concept is a precursor that is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature, commercially established, and independently reproduced everywhere. Recognition would be late but not premature.
uncertainties: Treatment of the Kazarinov-Suris 1971 proposal and Cho's role is unresolved.
Engineering impact may be viewed as stronger than fundamental physics novelty.
